_comment_headers: Header rules match the REQUEST path, not the file that ends up
being served. A rule on /index.html therefore never fires, because
visitors request / (and, via the SPA rewrite above, every other
path) -- those requests fell through to Firebase's default
max-age=3600, giving every visitor a one-hour stale window after a
deploy. Found by deploying and reading the response headers.
So: no-cache is the catch-all, and the content-hashed assets
override it. Assets are listed LAST because the last matching rule
wins; reversing these two would make every asset uncacheable.
